newsitem.title: FRANCE: French development aid to be 41 bln Ffr this year.
newsitem.headline: French development aid to be 41 bln Ffr this year.

text.p: France will spend some 41 billion francs on development aid this year after around 42 billion in 1996, and 40 billion in 1995 which made it second biggest Group of Seven donor that year, government officials said on Friday.

Following a recent OECD committee report commending its efforts in the domain, the officials said France was pushing to make sub-saharan Africa a key area of international government aid given its problems with access to private funding.
Private funding for development aid exceeds official aid by about three times, they noted.
France's 1995 aid contribution of 40 billion was in the form of bilateral aid to the tune of 30 billion and the rest was in multilateral aid, the officials noted.

As a percentage of gross domestic product, the contribution amounts to 0.55 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), putting France behind only Denmark, Norway, Sweden and the Natherlands out of the top 21 industrialised country donors.
In absolute terms, its 1995 contribution was second to top donor Japan and ahead of the United States.
